llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on thermoelectric materials for energy applications, with no biomedical context, no implant mechanics, no mechanical testing of porous structures, and no osseointegration considerations.

summary_zh.method: 粉末冶金表征与SLM工艺参数关联分析
summary_zh.result: 获得材料粉末特性对SLM成形质量的影响

summary_en.motivation: To characterize powder properties of thermoelectric materials for selective laser melting process optimization.
summary_en.method: Powder metallurgy characterization was performed and correlated with SLM processing parameters.
summary_en.result: The influence of powder characteristics on SLM build quality was identified.

papers.title: M2 macrophages contribute to osteogenesis and angiogenesis on nanotubular TiO
papers.abstract: The monocyte/macrophage system plays an essential role in the host response and the fate of endosseous implanted materials. Macrophage behavior was thought to be regulated by nanostructured titanium which has been considered as a very promising candidate for dental implants. However, there is little known for subsequent effects of these activated macrophages on osteogenesis and angiogenesis which were essential for bone integration. Here we presented two different dimensions of titanium nanotubes generated by anodic oxidation at 10 V (NT 10) and 20 V (NT 20), respectively. The behavior of macrophages on the surfaces was evaluated, and their conditioned medium (CM) was collected to stimulate MC3T3 and HUVECs, with commercially pure titanium (cp Ti) as control. We found that NT 20 induced macrophage activation similar to the anti-inflammatory M2 macrophage state with the enhanced expression of IL-10 and ARG, while NT 10 was associated with M1 macrophage phenotype characterized by high levels of IL-1β, iNOS and TNF-α. Furthermore, the osteogenic capacity of MC3T3 in CM from NT 20 was enhanced (NT 20 > NT 10 ≈ cp Ti) and the tube formation capacity of HUVECs was promoted in CM from nanotubular surfaces with increasing tube dimensions (NT 20 > NT 10 > cp Ti). Our data suggest that dental implants with the large nanotube dimension surface could result in a favorable osteoimmunomodulatory microenvironment for the establishment of osseointegration.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究纳米管TiO₂表面的巨噬细胞行为对成骨和血管生成的影响，与增材制造生物医学植入物的力学性能或疲劳无关。
llm.why_not_core: No LPBF fabrication, no mechanical testing (static or fatigue), no stress shielding or stiffness matching, and no as-built morphology characterization.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究纳米管态钛表面对巨噬细胞行为及其对骨整合的影响
summary_zh.method: 通过阳极氧化制备不同尺寸TiO₂纳米管，收集巨噬细胞条件培养基刺激成骨和内皮细胞
summary_zh.result: 大尺寸纳米管促进M2型巨噬细胞极化，增强成骨和血管生成能力
summary_zh.validation: 体外细胞实验验证巨噬细胞表型及条件培养基对成骨和血管生成的影响

summary_en.motivation: The study aims to investigate how nanotopography of titanium surfaces influences macrophage polarization and subsequent osteogenesis and angiogenesis for improved osseointegration.
summary_en.method: TiO2 nanotubes of two different diameters were fabricated via anodic oxidation; conditioned media from macrophages cultured on these surfaces were used to stimulate MC3T3 osteoblasts and HUVECs.
summary_en.result: Larger nanotubes (20 V) induced an M2-like anti-inflammatory macrophage phenotype, which enhanced osteogenic differentiation and tube formation compared to smaller nanotubes or smooth titanium.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell assays including cytokine expression profiling, osteogenic markers, and tube formation assays were performed.
